game: Week 6 TEN@IND / kickoff not in pack / IND -6.5 / total 43.5 / weather not saved

script.base: Book expects IND to lead: implied team totals about 25.0 IND and 18.5 TEN on a 43.5 total. Base flow is IND up by a score at half, Jonathan Taylor (58 carries, 208 rush yards over weeks 3-5) controlling the clock, and TEN tilting pass to Carnell Tate (26 targets, 375 air yards L3) and Wan'Dale Robinson (23 targets). Moderate pace, not a shootout; late IND run-lean with some TEN garbage-time throws.
script.flip1: Game stays inside one score into the fourth. Tony Pollard keeps a full share of his 47 L3 carries against IND's 5.21 YPC run defense and can clear a rush line without a pass-heavy script; Taylor's carry bump is smaller, so 89.5 rush and 112.5 rush+rec stay live unders.
script.flip2: IND jumps up 14+ early. TEN abandons the run and Pollard's rush line dies, while Ward throws into the environment where he has been bad (-0.23 EPA/dropback with no blitz vs IND's 20% blitz rate). Taylor's early grind may already be near 90 rush yards before kneeldowns, or clock-killing caps him. The other break is a shootout, which the 43.5 total says the book does not expect.

matchup.overlap: Best overlap is Tate (team-high 375 air yards, 26 targets, 209 rec yards L3) into IND's middle and explosive leak (8.72 YPA middle, 16 explosives). Pollard (47 carries, 174 yards) into IND's 5.21 YPC front is the other overlap, but the dog script fights it so it is not a selected leg. Taylor (58 carries, 208 yards, 3.59 YPC) runs into TEN's strength (3.78 YPC), which is the under case, not a bleed. Warren (179 rec yards) is IND's top receiver, but TEN middle at 8.03 YPA is not a special bleed.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Tate has been the passing game at 26 targets, 209 receiving yards and 375 air yards over the last 3 (about 70 yards a game) against a line of only 50, and a 6.5-point dog script should keep those targets coming into a defense allowing 8.72 YPA in the middle and 16 passes of 20+.
edge_players.must_be_true: Tate keeps about 8-9 targets and a full route share, and Ward converts enough of the 375-air-yard profile into actual yards rather than incompletions.
edge_players.kills_it: Ward's -0.23 no-blitz EPA meets IND's 20% blitz rate and the drive stalls; or the 209 yards are one boom game that cannot be split out; or a late inactive that is not in this pack.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Taylor has averaged about 69 rush yards plus 14 receiving yards (combined about 84) over the last 3, and TEN allows only 3.78 YPC, so a clock-control bump to about 22 carries at that efficiency plus his usual catches lands nearer 95-100 than 112.5.
edge_players.must_be_true: Receiving stays near the L3 role (11 targets, 43 yards, about 14 a game) and he does not break a long run; extra carries from an IND lead still leave cushion under 112.5.
edge_players.kills_it: TEN has allowed 14 runs of 10+; one 25-40 yard run plus 22-25 carries and a few checkdowns clears 112.5. Also dies if IND trails and the 11-target receiving role expands.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so step 8 cannot be run as specified. Counting stats agree with Taylor under: 208 rush + 43 rec over 3 games = 83.7/game vs 112.5, and TEN's 3.78 YPC supports the cap; price is -112, not a short alt. Tate's count also sits above the number (209/3 = 69.7 vs 50) but the listed price is +nan, so there is no no-vig to size. Disagreement on the strong Tate read: Ward is -0.23 EPA/dropback with no blitz and IND blitzes only 20%, so this defense is the split where the QB has been inefficient, and missing per-game splits mean the 70-yard average may be one explosive. That flags the strong read and does not cut it. Taylor is a lean with agreeing counts, so it stays. No model probability above 70% is claimed.

market_rung_price: carnelltate recyds over 50 (price not in pack, listed +nan, do not size); jonathantaylor rushrecyds under 112.5 at -112. No alt rungs in the pack. Not passing yards, TDs, or receptions.
pre_mortem: Monday the Tate over lost because IND sat back, blitzed on about a fifth of dropbacks, and Ward's no-blitz problems showed up as sacks and incompletions: Tate saw targets and finished in the 30s, and the 209-yard L3 was one long game plus two quiet ones this pack cannot split. The Taylor under lost the other way: IND led by two scores at half, Taylor already had a chunk run through a front that has given up 14 runs of 10+, then added swing passes and coasted past 112.5 combined while the team YPC still looked ordinary. The chunk-run counter is real, which is why Taylor is only a lean; the QB-EPA counter is why Tate is flagged rather than sized.
slip_story: One story: moderate IND lead on the -6.5 / 43.5 number, not a shootout and not a 21-point bury. TEN's offense pass-tilts to Tate so the recyds over lives on target volume; TEN's 3.78 YPC front keeps Taylor's rush+rec under 112.5 even with a carry bump. Do not add Pollard rush over (needs the competitive flip and IND's 5.21 YPC bleed) or Downs/Allen overs (need IND to throw, which a Taylor clock-control lead suppresses). One market per player, no TD legs. They correlate in the base script and split if IND buries TEN early (Taylor volume up, Tate still live in garbage time) or if Ward cannot complete anything (Tate dies, Taylor under still live).
